messages.subject: failed to plot due to the strange "Error in seq.int(0, to - from, by)  : 'to' must be finite" message
parts:
I've used ggplot2 to plot the power generated by our solar panels
since 11/01/2009. It has worked great except on 3 days (12/06, 12/16,
and 12/20) and produced no graphs. I looked at the error log but found
the following cryptic message:

-------------[ START LOG ]----------------
Sun Dec 20 22:00:01 PST 2009
Loading required package: proto
Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: plyr

Attaching package: 'ggplot2'


The following object(s) are masked from package:grid :

nullGrob

Error in seq.int(0, to - from, by) : 'to' must be finite
Calls: print ... <Anonymous> -> <Anonymous> -> fullseq_time ->
seq.POSIXt
Execution halted
1. Creating Now CVS data file...
2. Producing graphs and summary file...
Done.
-------------[ END LOG ]----------------

The line that caused the mysterious grief:

qplot(Time, Power.now, data = today, geom=c("point", "smooth"),
xlab="Time", ylab="Power (w)", main=today.title, span=0.3)

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: failed to plot due to the strange "Error in seq.int(0, to - from,  by) : 'to' must be finite" message
parts:
Hi Amanda,

The problem seems to be with the automatic tick mark selection. I've
been working with a grad student on a package for dealing with dates
that will eventually fix this problem and will hopefully make it into
a version of ggplot2 early next year. In the mean time, you can work
around it by explicitly specifying you want a tick every hour:

qplot(Time, Power.now, data = today) + scale_x_datetime(major = "hour")

Hadley

On Tue, Dec 22, 2009 at 5:05 PM, Amanda Chou <amand...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello Hadley,
>
> Thanks! I included the 12/20/2009 data file named "today" (very
> original, I know) by dput(). I just re-ran the qplot() command and got
> the same result, even if I dropped the "smooth" part.

> +   xlab="Time", ylab="Power (w)", main="Power Generated on
> 12-20-2009", span=0.3)

> Error in seq.int(0, to - from, by) : 'to' must be finite
>

> When I ran the regular not-too-exciting plot() command, it plotted
> dots all right:
>
>> plot(today$Time, today$Power.now, xlab="Time", ylab="Power (w)", main="Power Generated on 12-20-2009", type="p", pch=19)
>
> Thanks again! :)
>
> Amanda
